question: How many papers submitted to arXiv in November and December 2026 will mention agentic reinforcement learning in their abstracts?

calls.reasoning: The resolution search filters on most-recent-version submitted date, so a window queried right after it closes is at its largest (new papers plus revisions). Best analogs: Sep-Oct 2026 counted on Nov 1 = 221; Oct 2026 alone = 138. The count roughly doubled year over year (Nov-Dec 2025 = 106, though counted low because later revisions moved papers out). Nov should be boosted by ICLR rebuttal revisions; Dec is softer over the holidays. Projected Nov-Dec ≈ 250-300. Risks: the term plateaus or loses out to other wording; January revisions pull a few papers out before Metaculus queries. No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi.

calls.reconciliation: All three dossiers report identical window counts from the same query run on 2026-11-01, so there is no factual dispute to settle. The differences are judgment calls: (1) how strongly November ICLR-rebuttal revisions inflate the count (Run 1 high, Runs 2-3 moderate); (2) whether October's 138 was a one-off post-ICLR-deadline spike; (3) the size of the December dip; (4) the growth rate. The claim that submitted_date matches the latest version rests on one observed result in Runs 1 and 2 and is plausible. It implies the Sep-Oct=221 count, taken right after that window closed, is the right analog for how Metaculus will query Nov-Dec. Nov ≈ 130-150 plus Dec ≈ 100-125 gives about 255. Run 1's dispersion analysis is kept, slightly widened. The chance of exceeding 500 is small: it would need about a doubling in one window.
